purpose: Primary-source findings that change experiment selection, not a claim that paper headline gains transfer to this challenge.

sources.title: Understanding GPU Megakernels: Why Residency Can Mislead
sources.finding: Controlled H100 reconstructions retain operator code and required memory ordering. Separate kernels with PDL reduce TK decode latency 5.7% and match VDCores; runtime and completion-signal costs can outweigh persistent prefetch benefits.
sources.transfer: Check ready work, bottleneck bandwidth, and whole-CTA admission rather than treating idle SMs or more fusion as evidence of a gain. Preserve release/acquire ordering. Our decoder already uses PDL and only 7–10 kernels per layer, so a blind megakernel rewrite has no demonstrated ROI.

sources.title: One Megakernel is Not Enough: Predicting Where to Cut for Streaming Inference
sources.finding: Across NH-TTS, Qwen3-TTS and Llama-1B, the best tested composition ranges from zero to four megakernels. NH-TTS on H100 NVL with three specialized megakernels publishes first audio 21.4% sooner than one monolith.
sources.transfer: Use resource lifetimes, tile dependencies and measured service times to choose boundaries. This is streaming first-publication behavior on different models and hardware; 21.4% is not a Muse decoder prediction.

sources.title: ForgeMegakernel
sources.finding: Generates decode megakernels guided by structural milestones, precision contracts, byte accounting and an independent intermediate-state oracle. Conventional baselines issue 280–448 launches per decoded token on H100.
sources.transfer: Adopt its intermediate validation and evidence ledger. The baseline launch counts span a whole model, whereas our 7–10 counts are per layer and already fuse substantial work. Those counts alone neither prove nor quantify remaining fusion headroom.

sources.title: GC-MoE: Overlapping Expert-Parallel Token Dispatch with FP8/FP4 Grouped GEMM via CUDA Green Contexts
sources.finding: Separates communication and compute resource budgets using green contexts. Reported mean speedup on eight H20 GPUs is 1.188x versus its DeepGEMM baseline; Hopper uses register-A WGMMA with in-register FP4 decoding.
sources.transfer: Our one-GPU challenge omits communication, and this operator uses FP8 activations rather than required BF16 activations. Do not port its precision or claim the headline speedup. Resource isolation and exact scale-layout scheduling remain design references for a compact MoE implementation.

sources.title: ZipServ: Fast and Memory-Efficient LLM Inference with Hardware-Aware Lossless Compression
sources.finding: Uses tensor-core-aligned bitmap encoding and fused reconstruction directly into registers, avoiding full decompression to global memory. Main reported gains concern inference GPUs such as RTX4090, L40S and RTX5090.
sources.transfer: Our small-token dense kernels already use lossless 12-bit weights and direct reconstruction. This is not a novel blanket replacement or an H200 gain forecast. A different tile/resource pipeline must be distinguished from the incumbent before spending a GPU check.

next_direction: The highest-priority concrete design review is the author's compact two-consumer-warpgroup MoE CTA with enough actual shared-memory and register headroom for two resident CTAs. It must preserve total job weight reads, stage ownership, grid synchronization and BF16/FP32 precision. No performance claim or implementation approval follows merely from a 2-CTA target. Dense remains a necessary parallel portfolio target; no newly discovered dense mechanism yet supports a credible broad 25% gain.
